clue.text: Control irritating feeling after there's no escape from snow

indicators.note: the itch piece comes after the remains of the snow
the word no slips out of the word snow, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: an itch is an irritating feeling on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone longs to scratch an itch while stuck in a snowdrift with no way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no escape from snow' means NO is removed from SNOW, leaving SW; 'after' puts ITCH behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to operate or control something by flicking it on or off.

clue.text: Poor place to swap bits of drudgery

indicators.note: the two halves of the drudgery word change places

parts.note: housework is domestic drudgery

explanation.surface: A suggestion that chores be traded around at some miserable spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swap bits of' exchanges the two parts of HOUSEWORK, putting WORK before HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian workhouse was an institution housing the destitute, a place for the poor.

clue.text: Getting garden into shape, best not to open book

parts.note: the top is the best

indicators.note: the book word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a diary is a book of daily entries

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: best keep the book closed while tidying up the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to open' drops D, the first letter of DIARY, leaving IARY after TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping shrubs into ornamental shapes, giving a garden form.

clue.text: Shade if very extensive not good

indicators.note: the good letter is left out of the big word

parts.note: huge means very extensive

explanation.surface: A remark that a shady area, however large, may still be poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a colour or tint, the same sense as a shade of colour.

clue.text: Bomb massacre — a number lost in house

parts.note: the V1 was the German flying bomb of World War II, written VI

indicators.note: the number letter goes missing from the slaughter word

parts.note: carnage is a massacre
N stands for a number in algebra

explanation.surface: A bombing kills many people, and the death toll vanishes inside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes N out of CARNAGE to give CARAGE, after VI.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a vicar.

clue.text: Through beak, dove's taken up drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, taken up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the answer runs through the words beak and dove's

explanation.surface: A bird feeding a dove through its beak, which then takes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' marks the run AKDOV inside 'beak, dove's'; 'taken up' reverses it, as a down answer reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Policeman's expression of disgust to Lord David

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman
fie is an old exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A constable says something rude to a nobleman called David.
explanation.definitionFit: David Copperfield is the title hero of the Dickens novel, so his surname follows David.

clue.text: In tears, drunk —- on this?

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are rolling about out of order

explanation.surface: Someone weeping after too much wine, and the wine is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek resinated wine, a drink one might weep over when drunk.

clue.text: Revolver, say, raised? This makes things sticky

parts.note: a revolver is a gun

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards

parts.note: eg abbreviates for example, so says

explanation.surface: A question about a raised revolver, then a remark about something sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EG into GE under GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is sticky, messy stuff that coats things.

clue.text: Suddenly fail to appear so gorgeous

definitions.meaning: to die abruptly, so to fail suddenly
... gorgeous is a phrase for stunning good looks

explanation.definitionFit: Drop dead means to die suddenly, and drop-dead gorgeous describes striking beauty.

clue.text: Obvious man in hospital has heart failure

indicators.note: the middle letter of the hospital word fails, so it goes

parts.note: a patient is someone in hospital

explanation.surface: A man in hospital suffers heart failure, plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has heart failure' removes I, the central letter of PATIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or plain to see.

clue.text: He's a packet to distribute — but doesn't?

definitions.text: He's a packet to distribute — but doesn't?

indicators.note: distributing the letters spreads them into a new order

explanation.surface: A rich man who should hand his fortune out, but keeps it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who has money but will not spend or share it.

clue.text: Put up with raillery, letting attention go?

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it
raillery is teasing, read here as a tease

explanation.surface: Someone tolerating mockery calmly, without paying it attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting attention go' is the drill sense: soldiers move from attention to stand at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand at ease is the military order releasing soldiers from the position of attention.

clue.text: Charles is beheaded

indicators.note: the word for is loses its first letter

parts.note: to live is to be alive, so is can mean lives

explanation.surface: A grim report that a king Charles has been executed.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I was beheaded, but 'Charles' is Charles Ives, the American composer; 'beheaded' removes L from LIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer, so the surname answers the forename.

clue.text: Purchase -—- there's nothing in float

indicators.note: the nothing letter goes inside the purchase word

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A buyer finds nothing inside a float they have bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoy is a floating marker moored in water, a float.

clue.text: Trust deed?

parts.note: not a legal document setting up a trust, but a deed done out of trust or belief

explanation.definitionFit: An act of faith is something done purely out of trust, a deed of belief.

clue.text: Fish finally goes off in cask

indicators.note: the last letter of the fish word departs

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: Fish left in a barrel eventually rots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally goes off' drops A, the last letter of TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for wine or beer.

clue.text: Blunt and true: possibly describing Becket as priest?

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A blunt, honest judgement on Thomas Becket as a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry II reputedly asked to be rid of 'this turbulent priest', meaning Thomas Becket, Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Becket is famously called the turbulent priest, so the word describes him.

clue.text: Shaky performance from ringer Andy with changes at church

parts.note: a bell is something that rings

indicators.note: changes rearranges the name's letters, punning on bell-ringing changes

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer named Andy gives a wobbly display ringing changes at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with changes' turns ANDY into YDAN; 'at' just links to CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A belly dance is a performance with shaking hips and torso.

clue.text: Tend to save article, wipin memory

indicators.note: the lean word keeps the article safe inside it

parts.note: to lean is to tend or incline
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A carer tries to rescue a piece of writing while their memory fails.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper prints 'wipin', a typo for 'wiping'; the definition reads as wiping memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethe was the river of forgetfulness in Hades, so Lethean means causing loss of memory.

clue.text: I twisted round, strong and slim

indicators.note: the twisted word goes round the I

parts.note: wry means twisted, as a wry grin

explanation.surface: Someone turns round and shows a strong, slender figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiry describes a lean body that is also tough and sinewy.

clue.text: Sang of battles, and showed injury

parts.note: war is a series of battles
a cut that bled shows the injury

explanation.surface: A minstrel sang of war and wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To warble is to sing with trills, as a bird does.

clue.text: Tail's docked

parts.note: a short tail, as if cut off, like a rabbit's

explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short stubby tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: But Aintree jockeys often lose seat here

definitions.text: But Aintree jockeys often lose seat here

parts.words: But Aintree jockeys often lose seat here
parts.note: not a seat but a notorious Grand National fence where riders fall

explanation.definitionFit: The Chair is a huge fence at Aintree, Liverpool's Grand National course, and a chair is a seat.

clue.text: But such an expression unlikely to lighten?

definitions.text: But such an expression unlikely to lighten?

parts.words: But such an expression unlikely to lighten?
parts.note: a furious look rarely brightens, though thunder usually comes with lightning

explanation.surface: A glowering face that will not cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderous expression is a black, angry look, punning on thunder following lightning.

clue.text: Pigment not new in aggregate

indicators.note: the new letter is left out of the total word

parts.note: a number can be an aggregate or total

explanation.surface: A paint colour that is not fresh is found in a mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural brown earth pigment used in paints.

clue.text: A long time on river to get snapper

indicators.note: in an across answer on means placed after

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
an era is a long time

explanation.surface: A long fishing trip on the river to catch a snapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper is someone who snaps pictures, and by extension the device that takes them.

clue.text: Some looker —- there's beauty in her eyes

definitions.text: Some looker —- there's beauty in her eyes

parts.words: Some looker —- there's beauty in her eyes
parts.note: not a beautiful woman but the one looking, from the saying about beauty and eyes

explanation.definitionFit: Beauty is said to be in the eye of the beholder, one who looks at something.

clue.text: Popular with the retired, such bottled water?

definitions.text: with the retired, such bottled water?
definitions.meaning: people retiring to bed take a ...-water bottle

explanation.definitionFit: Hot means in demand, and a hot-water bottle warms those gone to bed.

clue.text: With regret, repelled by king's majesty

indicators.note: the king's letters come beside the rest, ahead of them

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
and can mean with

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the regret word reads backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A monarch's grandeur sours into regret and rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour or magnificence, close in sense to majesty.

clue.text: Fox took prey so far

parts.note: tod is a dialect word for a fox
a predator that took prey ate it

explanation.surface: A fox has had its meal so far.
explanation.definitionFit: To date means up to now, so far.
